extName.description: The extension name, in the browser and in both stores. A product name, left untranslated.

extDescription.message: Suggests which tabs to close, organizes the rest into native tab groups and blocks duplicate tabs in real time.
extDescription.description: The store description. Chrome Web Store allows at most 132 characters.

actionTitle.description: Tooltip on the toolbar icon, whose click opens the panel.

cmdCloseDuplicates.description: Name of the assignable keyboard shortcut, in the browser's shortcut page.

cmdToggleGuard.description: Name of the assignable keyboard shortcut, in the browser's shortcut page.

panelCounts.description: The header line that says how much is open, as in "87 tabs · 4 windows". Only the separator is translatable: both halves are already-formatted phrases.

countTabsOne.description: How many tabs are open, when there is exactly one. $1 is the formatted number.

countTabsOther.description: How many tabs are open, for every other count. $1 is the formatted number.

countWindowsOne.description: How many windows are open, when there is exactly one. $1 is the formatted number.

countWindowsOther.description: How many windows are open, for every other count. $1 is the formatted number.

navLabel.description: Accessible name of the panel's navigation bar, never shown on screen.

navDeclutter.description: Navigation tab for the view that suggests which tabs to close.

navOrganize.description: Navigation tab for the view that groups the remaining tabs.

navArchive.description: Navigation tab for the view that lists the tabs TabDeclutter closed.

navSettings.description: The gear button in the header, which opens the settings. Also its heading.

healthReview.description: How many tabs the score suggests looking at, next to the health bar. $1 is the formatted number.

declutterEmpty.message: All tidy. No tabs to review.
declutterEmpty.description: Shown in the Declutter view when the score suggests nothing.

declutterList.description: Accessible name of the Declutter list, never shown on screen: what a screen reader says when the keyboard enters it.

sectionDuplicates.description: Heading of the Declutter section holding tabs that show a page another tab already shows.

sectionTransient.description: Heading of the Declutter section holding pages that have already served their purpose: search results, sign-in pages, blank tabs.

sectionStaleUnread.description: Heading of the Declutter section holding tabs opened long ago and never actually looked at.

sectionStale.description: Heading of the Declutter section holding tabs the user has not come back to in a long time.

sectionReview.description: Heading of the Declutter section holding tabs with no single strong reason, only small signals. Folded by default.

sectionHeading.description: A section heading with how many tabs it holds, as in "Duplicates (3)". $1 is the section name, $2 the formatted count.

reasonDuplicate.description: The one-line reason under a tab's title, when another open tab shows the same page.

reasonBlank.message: Blank tab, open for a while
reasonBlank.description: The one-line reason under a tab's title, when the tab shows no page at all and has been idle for over an hour.

reasonTransient.description: The one-line reason under a tab's title, for a page that has served its purpose and is none of the more specific kinds below.

reasonSearch.message: Search results you already looked at
reasonSearch.description: The one-line reason under a tab's title, when the page is a search results page left behind.

reasonAuth.description: The one-line reason under a tab's title, when the page is a login, logout or OAuth callback page.

reasonBrowserPage.description: The one-line reason under a tab's title, when the page belongs to the browser itself, like its settings or downloads.

reasonStale.message: You have not opened it in $1
reasonStale.description: The one-line reason under a tab's title, when the tab is simply old. $1 is a duration, as in "12 days".

reasonStaleUnread.message: You have not opened it in $1 and never read it
reasonStaleUnread.description: The one-line reason under a tab's title, when the tab is old and was barely ever in the foreground. $1 is a duration, as in "12 days".

chipOpenedNever.description: Chip next to a tab's reason, when the tab was opened in the background and never brought to the front.

chipOpenedOne.description: Chip next to a tab's reason, when the tab was brought to the front exactly once. $1 is the formatted number.

chipOpenedOther.description: Chip next to a tab's reason, for every other number of times the tab was brought to the front. $1 is the formatted number.

chipBookmarked.description: Chip next to a tab's reason, when the page is already in the bookmarks, so closing the tab loses nothing.

chipNearDuplicate.description: Chip next to a tab's reason, when another open tab shows the same page bar the query string or the fragment.

chipDiscarded.description: Chip next to a tab's reason, when the browser has already dropped the page from memory.

chipError.description: Chip next to a tab's reason, when the page failed to load.

actionGo.description: Button on a tab's row that activates that tab and brings its window to the front.

actionKeep.description: Button on a tab's row and in the selection bar that keeps those tabs out of the suggestions for a week.

actionClose.description: Button on a tab's row that closes that tab.

actionDiscard.description: Button in the selection bar that drops the selected tabs from memory without closing them.

actionUndo.description: Button in the toast that appears after a close, bringing the tabs that were just closed back.

actionConfirm.description: Button that carries out a close the panel asked about first.

actionCancel.description: Button that dismisses a question the panel asked, leaving everything as it was.

rowSelect.description: Name of the checkbox on a tab's row, read by a screen reader. $1 is the tab's title.

sectionSelectAll.description: Button in a section's header that selects every tab of that section.

sectionDeselectAll.description: Button in a section's header, in place of "Select all" once every tab of that section is selected.

sectionCloseAll.description: Button in a section's header that closes every tab of that section. $1 is how many they are.

windowForgotten.description: Card above the Declutter list, offering a whole forgotten window. $1 is a counted noun, as in "12 tabs"; $2 a duration, as in "3 weeks".

windowClose.description: Button on the card above the Declutter list, which closes that whole forgotten window.

barLabel.description: Accessible name of the bar that appears at the bottom of the panel while tabs are selected, never shown on screen.

barClose.description: Button in the selection bar that closes the selected tabs. $1 is the formatted number.

barCloseWithWindows.description: Button in the selection bar when the selection empties one or more windows, so that it says what else goes. $1 is a counted noun, as in "3 tabs"; $2 is "the window" or "the windows".

barWindowOne.description: The second half of "Close 3 tabs and the window", when the selection empties exactly one window.

barWindowOther.description: The second half of "Close 8 tabs and the windows", when the selection empties more than one.

confirmClose.description: The question the selection bar asks before closing more than 25 tabs. $1 is a counted noun, as in "42 tabs".

confirmCloseActive.message: Close the tab you are using too?
confirmCloseActive.description: The question the selection bar asks when the close would take the tab the user is on right now.

toastClosedOne.description: The toast that appears after a close, when it was exactly one tab. $1 is the formatted number.

toastClosedOther.description: The toast that appears after a close, for every other count. $1 is the formatted number.

organizeEmpty.description: Shown in the Organize view when there is nothing to group.

organizeSkippedOne.description: Shown after applying the groups, when exactly one tab was closed or moved in the meantime. $1 is the formatted number.

organizeSkippedOther.description: Shown after applying the groups, for every other count of tabs left out. $1 is the formatted number.

organizeNoGroups.message: This browser cannot create tab groups.
organizeNoGroups.description: Shown in the Organize view when the browser has no native tab groups.

organizeScope.description: Accessible name of the Organize view's scope chooser.

organizeScopeWindow.description: Scope of the Organize view: only the tabs of the window the panel is in.

organizeScopeAll.description: Scope of the Organize view: the tabs of every window.

organizeScopeSelection.description: Scope of the Organize view: the tabs brought over from the selection bar. $1 is the formatted number.

organizeMode.message: How to group or sort your tabs
organizeMode.description: Accessible name of the Organize view's grouping mode chooser.

organizeModeSite.message: By website (e.g. keep all YouTube or GitHub tabs together)
organizeModeSite.description: Grouping mode: one group per site.

organizeModeTopic.message: By topic (tabs about the same subject across different sites)
organizeModeTopic.description: Grouping mode: groups of tabs that are about the same thing.

organizeOptions.description: Accessible name of the Organize view's options.

organizeOptionSort.message: Sort the tabs in the window by group
organizeOptionSort.description: Option of the Organize view: lay the tab strip out group by group.

organizeOptionCollapse.description: Option of the Organize view: create the groups collapsed.

organizeOptionLeavePinned.description: Option of the Organize view, on by default: pinned tabs are not grouped.

organizeOptionIncludeGrouped.message: Include tabs already in a group
organizeOptionIncludeGrouped.description: Option of the Organize view, off by default: tabs the user has already grouped are left alone.

organizePreview.description: Accessible name of the list of groups the Organize view proposes.

organizeGroupInclude.description: Accessible name of the checkbox that keeps a proposed group in or out.

organizeGroupName.description: Accessible name of the box that renames a proposed group.

organizeGroupColor.description: Accessible name of the chooser for a proposed group's colour.

organizeMoveTo.description: Menu on a tab in the preview that moves it to another proposed group.

organizeMerge.description: Menu on a proposed group that merges it into another one.

organizeOther.description: The tabs that stay out of every group, and the way to take a tab out of one.

organizeOtherHint.message: These tabs stay out of every group.
organizeOtherHint.description: Explains the "Other" list of the Organize view.

organizeWindow.description: Which window a proposed group belongs to, shown only when more than one is in scope. $1 is the number.

organizeApply.description: Button of the Organize view that creates the proposed groups in the browser.

organizeAppliedOne.description: Toast after applying, when exactly one group was created. $1 is the formatted number.

organizeAppliedOther.description: Toast after applying, for every other number of groups. $1 is the formatted number.

organizeDismiss.description: Accessible name of the button that closes the Organize view's toast without undoing.

organizeAiBadge.description: Badge shown on the Organize preview when the on-device model proposed the groups.

organizeAiUse.description: Checkbox of the Organize view that lets the on-device model group by topic.

organizeAiEnable.description: Button that starts the browser's one-off download of the on-device model.

organizeAiEnableHint.message: The browser downloads the model once; it is several gigabytes.
organizeAiEnableHint.description: Explains what turning on the on-device AI costs, next to the button that starts it.

organizeAiFallback.message: The on-device AI could not finish grouping, so local topic grouping was used instead. Your setting was kept.
organizeAiFallback.description: Warning shown in the Organize view when the on-device model fails or times out and local topic grouping is used without changing the user's AI preference.

organizeAiFallbackDetail.description: Short technical reason shown under the AI fallback warning so the user or developer can see why the browser's model fell back. $1 is the reason code or error.

organizeAiUnavailable.message: Chrome's on-device AI is currently unavailable, so local topic grouping will be used instead. Your setting was kept.
organizeAiUnavailable.description: Warning shown in the Organize view when the user enabled on-device AI but the browser currently reports the model as unavailable or unsupported.

organizeAiDownloading.description: Progress of the on-device model's download. $1 is the formatted percentage.

organizeAiWorking.message: The AI is grouping the tabs…
organizeAiWorking.description: Shown while the on-device model is being asked for the groups.

organizeAiCancel.description: Button that stops the on-device model and keeps the groups found without it.

barOrganize.description: Button in the selection bar that takes the selected tabs to the Organize view.

colorGrey.description: Name of a tab group colour.

colorBlue.description: Name of a tab group colour.

colorRed.description: Name of a tab group colour.

colorYellow.description: Name of a tab group colour.

colorGreen.description: Name of a tab group colour.

colorPink.description: Name of a tab group colour.

colorPurple.description: Name of a tab group colour.

colorCyan.description: Name of a tab group colour.

colorOrange.description: Name of a tab group colour.

archiveEmpty.description: Shown in the Archive view when nothing has been closed through TabDeclutter.

archiveNoMatch.description: Shown in the Archive view when the archive is not empty but the search and the filters leave no row.

archiveTools.description: Accessible name of the row holding the Archive view's search box and its two filters, never shown on screen.

archiveSearch.description: The Archive view's search box: its placeholder and its accessible name.

archiveWhen.description: Accessible name of the Archive view's date filter, never shown on screen.

archiveWhenAny.description: Option of the Archive view's date filter: no date restriction. The one it opens on.

archiveWhenToday.description: Option of the Archive view's date filter: closed today.

archiveWhenWeek.description: Option of the Archive view's date filter: closed in the last seven days, today included.

archiveWhenOlder.description: Option of the Archive view's date filter: closed more than seven days ago.

archiveOrigin.description: Accessible name of the Archive view's origin filter, never shown on screen.

archiveOriginAny.description: Option of the Archive view's origin filter: no restriction. The one it opens on.

archiveOriginMine.description: Option of the Archive view's origin filter: the tabs the user closed.

archiveOriginDuplicates.description: Option of the Archive view's origin filter: the tabs the duplicate guard closed on its own.

archiveList.description: Accessible name of the Archive view's list, never shown on screen.

archiveReasonManual.description: Why an archived tab was closed: the user closed it from the panel.

archiveReasonWindow.description: Why an archived tab was closed: it went with a whole window the user closed.

archiveReasonDuplicateAuto.description: Why an archived tab was closed: the duplicate guard closed it as it opened.

archiveReasonDuplicateManual.description: Why an archived tab was closed: the user closed it as a duplicate.

actionRestore.description: Button on an archived tab's row that opens it again.

actionDelete.description: Button on an archived tab's row that removes it from the archive for good.

archiveExport.description: Button in the Archive view that copies the rows on screen to the clipboard as a Markdown list of links.

archiveCopied.description: Confirmation shown after Export, under the Archive view's list.

archiveEmptyAll.description: Button in the Archive view that deletes every entry.

archiveConfirmEmpty.description: The question "Empty archive" asks before deleting everything. $1 is the formatted number of entries.

barRestore.description: Button in the Archive view's selection bar that opens the selected tabs again. $1 is the formatted number.

barDelete.description: Button in the Archive view's selection bar that removes the selected entries from the archive. $1 is the formatted number.

menuKeepAlways.description: Item in the right-click menu on a page or a tab: the tab is never suggested for closing again.

menuProtectSite.description: Item in the right-click menu on a page or a tab: the site joins the protected sites, and none of its tabs is ever suggested for closing.

menuAllowDuplicates.description: Item in the right-click menu on a page or a tab: the site joins the duplicate whitelist, so opening the same page twice is no longer blocked.

menuReopenDuplicate.description: Item in the menu on the extension icon: brings back the tab the duplicate guard closed most recently, and does not close it again.

menuReopenAllowSite.message: …and always allow duplicates for this site
menuReopenAllowSite.description: Item in the menu on the extension icon: reopens the last duplicate closed and adds its site to the duplicate whitelist.

menuPauseGuard.description: Parent item in the menu on the extension icon: holds the three pause durations below.

menuPause15Min.description: Pause duration under 'Pause duplicate protection' in the menu on the extension icon.

menuPause1Hour.description: Pause duration under 'Pause duplicate protection' in the menu on the extension icon.

menuPauseRestart.description: Pause duration under 'Pause duplicate protection' in the menu on the extension icon: the pause lasts until the browser is restarted.

guardChip.description: The duplicate-protection chip in the panel's header. $1 is the state: ON, Warnings only, OFF, or paused.

guardStateOff.description: State in the duplicate-protection chip: no live checks at all.

guardStateWarn.description: State in the duplicate-protection chip: duplicates are reported but never closed.

guardStateAuto.description: State in the duplicate-protection chip: duplicates are closed automatically.

guardStatePausedUntil.description: State in the duplicate-protection chip while it is paused. $1 is a clock time, such as 15:40.

guardStatePausedRestart.description: State in the duplicate-protection chip while it is paused until the browser is restarted.

guardMenuLabel.description: Name of the menu that opens from the duplicate-protection chip, for screen readers.

guardMenuResume.description: Menu item on the duplicate-protection chip that ends the pause immediately.

guardMenuCloseAll.description: Menu item on the duplicate-protection chip that closes every duplicate tab. $1 is how many would close.

guardMenuSettings.description: Menu item on the duplicate-protection chip that opens the duplicate settings.

guardClosedTodayOne.description: Counter under the chip after the protection closes a tab, when the count is one. $1 is the number.

guardClosedTodayOther.description: Counter under the chip after the protection closes a tab. $1 is the formatted number.

guardNoticeSee.description: Link beside the counter under the chip: opens the archive filtered to the duplicates closed automatically.

settingsGroupSuggestions.description: Heading of the first group of settings: what makes a tab a candidate for closing.

settingsFieldStale.message: Close unused tabs not opened for more than
settingsFieldStale.description: Settings field that chooses how long a tab must go unused before it counts as old.

settingsFieldGrace.message: Never touch newly opened tabs for at least
settingsFieldGrace.description: Settings field that chooses the grace period: a tab opened more recently than this is never suggested.

settingsIncludeGrouped.message: Include tabs that are in a group
settingsIncludeGrouped.description: Settings checkbox: whether tabs already in a tab group can be suggested.

settingsIncludeGroupedHint.message: They are suggested less readily, because a group is a decision.
settingsIncludeGroupedHint.description: Explanation under the 'Include tabs that are in a group' checkbox.

settingsIgnoreHashHint.message: Same setting as in the duplicate protection.
settingsIgnoreHashHint.description: Explanation under the 'Ignore #hash' checkbox, which is shown on both settings pages.

settingsBookmarks.message: Recognize pages already saved in Bookmarks
settingsBookmarks.description: Settings checkbox: whether a bookmarked page is more readily suggested, since closing it loses nothing.

settingsBookmarksHint.message: If a tab is already saved in your Bookmarks it can be closed sooner when unused, since you already have it saved.
settingsBookmarksHint.description: Explanation under the 'Use the bookmarks' checkbox.

settingsBookmarksDenied.message: Without permission to read the bookmarks they cannot be used. You can turn this on again at any time.
settingsBookmarksDenied.description: Message shown when the user refuses the browser's permission request for the bookmarks.

settingsGroupProtected.description: Heading of the group of settings that lists the sites which are never suggested.

settingsProtectedHint.message: Tabs on these websites will never be closed or suggested for cleanup. Type one domain per line (e.g. mail.google.com or *.github.com).

settingsProtectedLabel.description: Label of the text box in which the protected sites are typed, one per line.

settingsGroupGeneral.description: Heading of the group of settings that are neither about the suggestions nor about a site: badge, AI, archive, language.

settingsGroupExperimental.description: Heading of the collapsible experimental settings section at the bottom of Settings.

settingsExperimentalAiHint.message: Optional and Chrome-only. Local organization already runs instantly and offline without AI.
settingsExperimentalAiHint.description: Honest explanation under the Experimental heading clarifying that on-device AI is optional and off by default.

settingsShowBadge.message: Show the number of tabs to clean up on the toolbar icon
settingsShowBadge.description: Settings checkbox: whether the toolbar icon carries the count of tabs worth reviewing.

settingsUseAi.description: Settings checkbox: whether the browser's own on-device model may be used to name the groups.

settingsAiAvailable.description: State line under the on-device AI setting, when the browser has the model ready.

settingsAiDownloadable.message: On-device model: to download. It is downloaded the first time you use it.
settingsAiDownloadable.description: State line under the on-device AI setting, when the browser can download the model.

settingsAiUnsupported.message: On-device model: not supported by this browser.
settingsAiUnsupported.description: State line under the on-device AI setting, when the browser has no on-device model.

settingsFieldRetention.message: Keep closed tabs saved in the Archive for
settingsFieldRetention.description: Settings field that chooses how long closed tabs stay in the archive.

settingsFieldLanguage.description: Settings field that chooses the language of the extension.

settingsLanguageAuto.description: Language option: follow the browser's language.

settingsLanguageIt.description: Language option: Italian. Written in Italian in every language, as language lists do.

settingsOpenDuplicates.description: Button at the end of the settings that opens the duplicate-protection sub-page.

settingsBack.description: Button that goes back from the duplicate-protection sub-page to the main settings page.

settingsDuplicates.description: Heading of the duplicate-protection settings page.

guardGroupBehaviour.description: Heading of the first group of duplicate settings: what happens when a duplicate is found.

guardGroupPriority.description: Heading of the group of duplicate settings that decide which tab stays open.

guardGroupPriorityHint.message: They decide which tab stays open.
guardGroupPriorityHint.description: Explanation under the 'Priority and exclusions' heading.

guardGroupMatch.description: Heading of the group of duplicate settings that define when two URLs count as the same.

guardGroupMatchHint.message: Defines what counts as a duplicate, in Declutter too.

guardGroupWhitelist.description: Heading of the duplicate whitelist: the URLs for which duplicates are always allowed.

guardGroupWhitelistHint.message: URLs for which duplicates are always allowed.

guardFieldMode.description: Label of the setting that chooses what the protection does.

guardModeOff.description: Value of 'When a duplicate is detected': no live checks.

guardModeWarn.description: Value of 'When a duplicate is detected': report the duplicate but never close it.

guardModeAuto.description: Value of 'When a duplicate is detected': close the duplicate tab.

guardFieldAfter.description: Label of the setting that chooses what happens to the tab that was kept.

guardAfterNone.description: Value of 'On the remaining tab': leave it where it is.

guardAfterActivate.description: Value of 'On the remaining tab': bring it to the foreground.

guardAfterMoveActivate.message: Move it to the closed tab's position and activate it
guardAfterMoveActivate.description: Value of 'On the remaining tab': move it where the closed tab was, then activate it.

guardFieldScope.description: Label of the setting that chooses how far the protection looks for duplicates.

guardScopeWindow.description: Value of 'Where to look': only tabs of the same window are duplicates.

guardScopeAllWindows.description: Value of 'Where to look': tabs of any window are duplicates.

guardFieldKeep.description: Label of the setting that chooses which of two duplicates stays open.

guardKeepOldest.description: Value of 'Which tab to keep': the one opened first.

guardKeepNewest.description: Value of 'Which tab to keep': the one opened last.

guardKeepOldestReloaded.message: The oldest, reloaded with the new URL
guardKeepOldestReloaded.description: Value of 'Which tab to keep': keep the first tab but load the URL of the newer one in it.

guardPreferHttps.message: Prefer the HTTPS tab, and treat http and https as equivalent

guardKeepActive.message: Keep the active tab, the one you are working on

guardPreferActiveWindow.message: Prefer the active window, with the 'All windows' scope

guardIgnoreEmptyTabs.message: Ignore empty tabs, such as about:blank and the new tab page

guardIgnoreAuthPages.message: Ignore sign-in and OAuth pages, so logins are not interrupted

guardAllowIntentional.message: Allow duplicates made on purpose with 'Duplicate tab'
guardAllowIntentional.description: Checkbox among the duplicate exclusions. Only shown where the browser lets the extension recognise that command.

guardContainersSeparate.message: Treat containers as separate: the same URL in two containers is not a duplicate
guardContainersSeparate.description: Checkbox among the duplicate exclusions. Only shown in browsers that have containers.

matchIgnoreCase.message: Ignore upper and lower case in the URL
matchIgnoreCase.description: Checkbox among the URL comparison options.

matchIgnoreWww.description: Checkbox among the URL comparison options.

matchIgnoreHash.message: Ignore #hash, except app routes such as #/page
matchIgnoreHash.description: Checkbox among the URL comparison options.

matchIgnoreTracking.message: Ignore tracking parameters, such as utm_source and fbclid
matchIgnoreTracking.description: Checkbox among the URL comparison options.

matchIgnoreAllParams.description: Checkbox among the URL comparison options.

matchIgnorePath.message: Ignore the path, comparing the domain only
matchIgnorePath.description: Checkbox among the URL comparison options.

guardWarnNewest.message: With 'The newest' the protection can close a tab you were working on.
guardWarnNewest.description: Warning shown in the settings when the tab kept is the newest one.

guardWarnIgnorePath.message: Ignoring the path is very aggressive: two different pages of the same site count as duplicates.
guardWarnIgnorePath.description: Warning shown in the settings when only the domain is compared.

whitelistLabel.description: Label of the duplicate whitelist editor.

whitelistHint.message: * stands for any text. A line between slashes, /…/, is a regular expression.
whitelistHint.description: Explanation under the duplicate whitelist editor's label.

whitelistSave.description: Button that saves the duplicate whitelist as it has been typed.

whitelistDefaults.description: Button that puts this browser's default patterns back into the whitelist editor.

whitelistLine.description: Prefix of the feedback under the whitelist editor. $1 is the line number.

whitelistIgnored.description: Feedback for a whitelist line that does not compile. $1 is the reason.

whitelistMatchesNone.description: Feedback for a whitelist line that currently matches nothing.

whitelistMatchesOne.description: Feedback for a whitelist line that matches exactly one tab. $1 is the number.

whitelistMatchesOther.description: Feedback for a whitelist line and how many open tabs it matches. $1 is the formatted number.

whitelistErrorTooLong.description: Why a whitelist line was ignored.

whitelistErrorTooManyWildcards.description: Why a whitelist line was ignored.

whitelistErrorInvalidRegex.description: Why a whitelist line was ignored.

onboardingIntro.message: TabDeclutter suggests which tabs to close and helps you organize the rest. Everything stays on your device.
onboardingIntro.description: First sentence of the first-run screen.

onboardingThreshold.description: Field of the first-run screen that chooses the age threshold.

onboardingGuard.message: When you open a tab that is already open
onboardingGuard.description: Question of the first-run screen about duplicate protection.

onboardingGuardAuto.message: Close it and go back to the existing one
onboardingGuardAuto.description: Answer to the first-run duplicate question: close duplicates automatically.

onboardingGuardWarn.description: Answer to the first-run duplicate question: report duplicates but never close them.

onboardingGuardOff.description: Answer to the first-run duplicate question: no live checks at all.

onboardingPartialData.message: In the first few days the suggestions are based on partial data and get more accurate as you use it.
onboardingPartialData.description: Note of the first-run screen about what the suggestions are worth at the start.

onboardingStart.description: Button that saves the first-run choices and opens the panel.

autopilotTitle.description: Heading of the autopilot controls card.

autopilotHint.message: Keep your browser tidy automatically in the background.
autopilotHint.description: Subtitle of the autopilot controls card.

autopilotDeclutter.message: Auto-close useless and old tabs (saved to Archive)

autopilotOrganize.description: Toggle for automatic background window and tab organization.

windowModeHeading.description: Heading for the switch between the two window organization modes.

windowModeMergeTitle.message: Merge and tidy into a single window
windowModeMergeTitle.description: Option 1: consolidate multiple windows into one sorted window.

windowModeMergeHint.message: Combines scattered windows into one clean window and sorts tabs side by side by website or topic (without creating coloured tab groups).

windowModeSplitTitle.message: One window per topic or website
windowModeSplitTitle.description: Option 2: place each topic/site cluster into its own dedicated window.

windowModeSplitHint.message: Moves related tabs into dedicated windows so each Chrome window covers one coherent topic or project (without coloured tab groups).

windowOrganizeNow.description: Button that runs window organization immediately.

windowOrganizedOne.description: Toast after organizing windows into one clean window. $1 is the formatted count.

windowOrganizedOther.description: Toast after organizing tabs across multiple windows. $1 is the formatted count.

windowUngroupAll.description: Button that dissolves all existing Chrome tab groups.

windowUseTabGroups.description: Optional toggle to enable native tab groups.

windowUseTabGroupsHint.message: Choose 'By website' to keep pages from the same site together, or 'By topic' to group pages about the same subject.
windowUseTabGroupsHint.description: Explanation under the organizeMode / useTabGroups control.

declutterIntro.message: Tabs you probably no longer need. Close them in one click or turn on Autopilot above: every closed tab is saved in the Archive.
declutterIntro.description: Introductory helper text at the top of the Declutter view.

declutterCloseRecommended.description: Primary one-click button to close all tabs in the close bucket. $1 is the formatted count.

organizeIntro.message: Keep your Chrome windows tidy automatically without cluttering the tab bar with coloured groups.
organizeIntro.description: Introductory helper text at the top of the Organize view.

archiveIntro.message: Every tab closed by you or by Autopilot is kept here so you can restore it anytime.
archiveIntro.description: Introductory helper text at the top of the Archive view.
